newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan mulls delaying satellite launch.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan mulls delaying satellite launch.

text.p: Taiwan said on Monday it may postpone a scheduled 1998 launch of the island's first satellite, the ROCSAT-1, due to severe technical problems.
"My personal judgement and evaluation is that (the launch) may be delayed," Liu Chao-shiuan, chairman of the cabinet-level National Science Council, told a parliament sub-committee.

"The design will not necessarily cause the satellite to explode within 15 seconds, but since it has the potential risk, we must try to fix the problems and reduce such risk to the minimum level," Liu said.
His comments were carried on state-funded television.
Taiwan has planned to launch ROCSAT-1 in April 1998 from Cape Canaveral in Florida.
The council has found some technical problems related to coupled loads between the satellite and its launching vehicle, which are built by two different companies.
The problems, if unsolved, could cause explosion within 15 seconds after its launch, space experts have warned.

Taiwan has signed a US$61 million contract with TRW Inc of the United States to design and build the ROCSAT-1 satellite. It awarded a US$18 million contract to U.S.-based Lockheed Missiles and Space Company for the satellite's launching vehicle.
The National Space Programme Office said in July that TRW and Lockheed were studying the problems and it did not expect the project to be delayed.
Under a $516 million space programme, Taiwan plans to have three scientific research and communications satellites in orbit by 2006.
